summary: All pages remain visually intact across desktop and mobile with perfect accessibility, best-practices, and SEO scores. Mobile performance improved across the board — the homepage climbed to 85 and both project-detail pages rose to 80 — but note-structurer and screenshot-to-primevue remain below the 85 threshold, driven by LCPs above 4.3 s.

pages.visual_fingerprint: Full-page portfolio homepage with teal-accented hero ('App Design' heading, 'Send Me a Message' CTA), four dark content sections (pillars, timeline, case studies, skills, conferences, contact form), and a dark contact footer — all sections visible and correctly laid out on both desktop and mobile.

About page with shared nav, 'About Me' hero, two-column bio + dark-themed code snippet panel, 12+/16+/2/7 stats row, engineering culture section (with notable whitespace on desktop), and a dark contact footer — correctly rendered on both desktop and mobile.

Fully styled projects index with 'My Projects' heading, 'Latest Builds' featured row (Token Field, Noise Translator, Tail Risk Lab), seven project cards in a multi-column desktop grid collapsing to single-column on mobile, and a dark contact footer — correctly rendered on both desktop and mobile.

Clinical Note Structurer detail page with breadcrumb nav, 'Evals: 10/10 passing' badge, amber disclaimer banner, two-column visit note / structured result interactive demo (stacked to single-column on mobile), expandable JSON and HIPAA architecture accordions, and a dark contact footer — correctly rendered on both desktop and mobile.

Screenshot → PrimeVue detail page with breadcrumb nav, 'Evals: 5/5 passing' badge, dashed-border image drop zone, three sample thumbnail cards (Login form, Analytics dashboard, Pricing page) visible on both desktop and mobile with third card wrapping to its own row on mobile, a placeholder result panel, expandable accordions, and a dark contact footer — correctly rendered on both desktop and mobile.

top_fix: LCP remains above 4.3 s on both project-detail pages, keeping their mobile performance scores at 80 — preload each page's hero/LCP element with `<link rel="preload" fetchpriority="high">`, serve all images as WebP at display dimensions, and defer non-critical JS; this is the single change most likely to push note-structurer and screenshot-to-primevue above the 85 performance threshold.
